audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers tell you to dodge or outrun Twisted Advance: 'dodge his root' (tldr), 'His lock-on root. Dodge it.' (dosFull), 'use Move Quick to escape Twisted Advance's root dash' (wants.you[2]), 'Move Quick lets you simply walk away from Twisted Advance' (mid). Twisted Advance is a targeted dash — Maokai contorts into roots and dashes TO the target. It does not miss and it cannot be sidestepped once cast.
audit.why: This is the matchup's headline instruction and it is not a thing the player can do. Worse, it will get him killed at exactly the moment he thinks he is safe: he sees the cast, tries to walk, and is rooted anyway with his disengage already spent.
audit.corrected: You cannot dodge it. You stay outside its 525 range, or you accept the root and make sure Move Quick is still available for what comes after it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/maokai.json (W Twisted Advance: 'dashing to the target. Upon arrival, he roots the target', range 525)

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing states that Maokai is untargetable for the duration of the Twisted Advance dash.
audit.why: It directly changes when Blinding Dart can be spent. A Teemo who reacts to the cast by throwing Q at him is throwing it at an untargetable champion. The blind has to be pre-spent before he commits, or held until he has landed.
audit.corrected: He is untargetable mid-dash. Blind before he casts or after he arrives — never during.
sources: champ-data/_kits/maokai.json (W Twisted Advance: 'becoming untargetable and dashing to the target', untargetable flag)

audit.whatIsWrong: 'early' states 'his passive only procs off allied spell hits, not your attacks on him'. Sap Magic reads the other way: 'Each time Maokai casts a spell or is struck by an ENEMY's spell, this cooldown is reduced.'
audit.why: It is backwards, and the truth is a real cost the player should be weighing. Every Blinding Dart and every mushroom that lands on Maokai accelerates his passive back off cooldown, which means chip-spamming him with spells partly pays for his own sustain. That argues for attack-poison poke over spell spam, which is the opposite of what the current text implies.
audit.corrected: Your spells hitting him bring Sap Magic back faster. The heal itself comes from his basic attack, so blind is what actually denies it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nature's Grasp is not mentioned anywhere in the content layer, and the full layer only refers to 'his ultimate' generically.
audit.why: It is a 3000-range advancing wall of brambles that roots everything in its path, and Teemo owns no dash. This is the flagged missing interaction for the matchup: it does not threaten your health, it threatens your exit, and the answer is to hold Flash for the wall rather than for the damage.
audit.corrected: Nature's Grasp, 130/110/90s, travels 3000 and roots on contact. Against a champion with no dash it is a retreat-cutter, not a damage tool.
sources: champ-data/_kits/maokai.json (R Nature's Grasp, range 3000, hardCC, terrain)

audit.whatIsWrong: Sapling Toss is mentioned only as generic 'sapling chip'. Its range (1100) and the 'more effective in brush' clause are both absent.
audit.why: 1100 is far outside anything Teemo has — his Q is 680 — so saplings are how Maokai touches him without ever entering the trade. And because they are stronger in brush, the bushes Teemo wants to sit in are the exact ground the ability is designed to deny. The 'mid' section warns about brush but blames Twisted Advance for it, which is the wrong ability.
audit.corrected: Sapling Toss: 18-14s, 1100 range, and explicitly stronger in brush. That is the brush-denial tool, not W.
sources: champ-data/_kits/maokai.json (E Sapling Toss, range 1100, cd 18/17/16/15/14, 'More effective in brush')

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[3] claims 'Max-rank Blinding Shot now covers a 12-second window where Maokai physically cannot auto you' at Levels 4-5.
audit.why: Three problems in one clause: Q rank 5 needs level 9; Q's cooldown is a flat 7s at every rank, so it can never cover a 12-second window; and the sentence is using an invented blind duration as if it were uptime. The stage it describes is the stage the whole entry rests on.
audit.corrected: Q is rank 3 at best here, on a flat 7s cooldown, and the blind lasts a fraction of that.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[2] says Maokai should 'Stack Bramble Vest early to reduce your Toxic Shot on-hit damage and passive healing denial'.
audit.why: Toxic Shot is magic damage; Bramble Vest is armour and does nothing to it. The Grievous Wounds on Bramble Vest is also irrelevant, because Teemo does not heal. The item is close to a dead buy against this specific Teemo and the entry recommends it as his counterplay.
audit.corrected: Armour does not touch magic poison. His real answer is magic resist plus the Sap Magic heal, which is why blind matters more than raw poke here.
sources: champ-data/_kits/teemo.json (E Toxic Shot, magic on-hit poison)

audit.why: 51.41% over 319 games, and both charts give Teemo the middle stages with the late game levelling off. This is one of the few matchups in my slice where the level chart and the win rate point the same direction.

edits.before: Maokai's sapling toss and passive sustain let him contest the first wave — he heals off your poke faster than you expect at level 1, so don't over-commit your E stacks before you have Q.
edits.after: Sapling Toss throws 1100 and is explicitly stronger in brush — far outside your 680, and aimed at exactly the bushes you want to sit in. Take the CS at range and do not contest the first wave.

edits.before: Maokai's tankiness catches up to your damage output at full build — neither side can close, so the lane becomes a macro contest around who controls side-wave tempo and vision.
edits.after: Nature's Grasp travels 3000 and roots through anything, and you have no dash. At 2+ items it is not a damage threat, it is a retreat-cutter — hold Flash for the wall, not for the burst.

edits.before: Maintain level advantage with priority and use Move Quick to escape Twisted Advance's root dash
edits.after: Hold the 525 line — Twisted Advance is targeted and cannot be dodged once he has cast it

edits.before: Stack Bramble Vest early to reduce your Toxic Shot on-hit damage and passive healing denial
edits.after: Build magic resist rather than Bramble Vest — armour does nothing to a magic poison

edits.before: Maokai's passive heals off sapling and ability hits from level 1, and you have no blind yet to stop his auto-retaliations — accept a neutral first wave rather than trading into his sustain.
edits.after: Sapling Toss reaches 1100 and is stronger in brush, so he touches you from outside every range you own and denies the bushes you want — take a neutral first wave rather than contesting it.

edits.before: Blinding Shot cancels his auto-based passive healing trigger entirely, and his Twisted Advance is on a long cooldown at level 2 — this is your first real edge and the start of your poke loop.
edits.after: Blinding Dart denies the Sap Magic heal, because that heal rides on his basic attack — but remember your spells landing on HIM speed the passive back up, so poke with attacks, not darts.

edits.before: Max-rank Blinding Shot now covers a 12-second window where Maokai physically cannot auto you, and your poison DoT runs the full duration while his passive sustain stays dormant — freeze and deny freely.
edits.after: Q is rank 3 at best here on a flat 7s cooldown — there is no 12-second blind window anywhere in this. What you actually own is range: he has to enter 525 to root you, and that is a long walk through poison.

edits.before: At level 1 Maokai wins the passive sustain race — his sapling bounces off minions and heals off every ability hit, so if you try to brawl the very first wave with E autos you will trade even or slightly behind. Hold back, last-hit at your auto range, and wait for level 2. The moment you hit Q, the entire dynamic flips: Blinding Shot erases his auto-trade window completely, and his passive cannot heal off attacks he cannot land. From level 2 onward, stand at the edge of your Toxic Shot range, poke one or two E autos, then Q-blind when he walks up to retaliate — his passive only procs off allied spell hits, not your attacks on him, so your DoT stacks accumulate while his sustain sits idle.
edits.after: At level 1 Maokai wins the sustain race and out-ranges you doing it — Sapling Toss throws 1100 against your 680, and it is explicitly stronger in brush, so the bushes are his ground and not yours. Hold back, last-hit at range, and wait for level 2 rather than contesting anything. From there Blinding Dart earns its cooldown, because the Sap Magic heal rides on his basic attack and blind is what erases basic attacks. One caveat the old advice had exactly backwards: Sap Magic comes off cooldown FASTER when he is struck by an enemy spell, which means your darts and your mushrooms landing on him partly pay for his own sustain. Poke with attacks and poison, and spend Q on his step-up.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 6 are your strongest zone-control window. Q is nearly max rank, your poison chip forces him below the all-in threshold before he can reach you, and Move Quick lets you simply walk away from Twisted Advance if he ever overextends to try the root. The danger is getting cocky into brush: Maokai's W roots through vision and he will walk up to a bush and W-dash faster than you can react if you are standing still in your invisible camouflage — always break invisibility by moving before his W animation locks onto you. Shroom the river bushes and tribush at level 6 so any Twisted Advance approach lights him up for your team.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 are your control window, but not because of blind uptime — Q is rank 3 on a flat 7s cooldown and nothing about that changes. It is because Twisted Advance only reaches 525, and 525 is a long walk into your poison. Be clear about what it is, though: a targeted dash. You cannot sidestep it, and Move Quick does not outrun it, so the answer is the range line rather than reflexes. He is also untargetable for the whole dash, so a Q thrown at him mid-flight is simply a wasted Q — blind before he commits, or after he lands. Shroom the river bushes and the tribush at 6 so the approach lights him up before he arrives.

edits.before: Build MR — shroom %HP-poke, dodge his root. Teemo wins the Twisted Advance cooldown windows.
edits.after: Build MR — shroom-poke, stay outside his 525. Teemo wins the Twisted Advance windows.

edits.before: - Maokai Twisted Advance: matchup-defining — His lock-on root. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Maokai Twisted Advance 14-10s at 525: targeted, so you cannot dodge it — stay outside the range instead. - Sapling Toss 18-14s at 1100, stronger in brush. - Nature's Grasp 130/110/90 travels 3000 and cuts your exit.

edits.before: Q-blind erases his auto-trade window entirely. Only take the trade when Maokai's Twisted Advance is down.
edits.after: Q-blind erases the Sap Magic heal — it rides on his attack. Trade when Twisted Advance is down.

edits.before: His lock-on root. Dodge it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Targeted root — undodgeable. Hold the 525 line instead of reacting.

edits.before: Maokai wastes Twisted Advance (Root) — commit the full pattern immediately.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.

notes: Headline correction: BOTH layers instruct the player to dodge Twisted Advance ('dodge his root', 'His lock-on root. Dodge it.', 'Move Quick lets you simply walk away from Twisted Advance'). It is a targeted dash — it cannot be dodged, and the guide's own dosFull line calls it a 'lock-on root' in the same sentence that says to dodge it. The correct instruction is a range discipline (525), which is a different behaviour entirely. Second: 'early' asserts Maokai's passive 'only procs off allied spell hits, not your attacks on him'. Sap Magic's cooldown is reduced when he is struck by an ENEMY's spell, i.e. yours — so the text is backwards and the real consequence (spell chip partly funds his sustain, attack-poison chip does not) is genuinely counter-intuitive and worth keeping. Third: Nature's Grasp appears nowhere in the content layer despite being the flagged missing interaction for this pairing and the only thing in his kit that punishes Teemo's lack of a dash. Champion-wide name defects still outstanding: "Blinding Shot" x271 and "Liandry's Angueur" x80 in champ-data/content/teemo.js.
